claim: Active alignment brings the system into conformance with new or previously violated obligations. Retained models and mechanisms then support passive preservation and become capital when later work benefits.
topology: Two sequential panels; active compare/modify/evaluate feedback then passive change/evaluate feedback with retained models.
required_terms: Once active alignment succeeds, retain the models and mechanisms.
Models, mechanisms, and governance remain as engineering capital for every change.
bw_encoding: Light-gray panels distinguish the two alignment modes; stacks denote retained models.
redesign: Author approved after deleting the bottom engineering-capital footer and replacing the caption retention sentence with the point that retained models, mechanisms, and governance become capital when subsequent changes benefit.
alt: Two stacked shaded panels. Active alignment uses models with new obligations to compare and detect gaps, modify the system with agents, and evaluate and check alignment, repeating until correspondence and producing an aligned system. Retain the models and mechanisms after success. Passive alignment evaluates proposed changes against the same models and known obligations, admitting or rejecting changes and continuing to protect correspondence. The retained models, mechanisms, and governance are engineering capital for subsequent changes.
